title: Two Indians Among 11 Injured as Houthis Strike Riyadh Finance District Tower
excerpt: Saudi Civil Defence said a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District was hit in a terrorist attack on Tuesday. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed two Indian nationals were injured and said assistance is being extended to them and their families.
body:
• Eleven people were injured on Tuesday, November 24, when a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was targeted in what Saudi Civil Defence called a terrorist attack by Yemen's Houthi militia.
  • The injured include two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, according to Saudi Civil Defence.
  • The Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed the two injured Indians, said further details are being ascertained, and promised all possible assistance to the injured and their families.
  • For Indians in Saudi Arabia: the embassy has asked Indian nationals to abide by local rules and regulations, and families seeking information should contact the Indian Embassy in Riyadh, which is coordinating assistance.

Two Indian nationals were among 11 people injured on Tuesday when a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under attack, Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said, describing the strike as a "terrorist attack" by Yemen's Houthi militia. The financial district is the Saudi capital's main banking and business hub.

Those injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, the Civil Defence said. It added that the competent authorities responded immediately, implemented the approved procedures for such incidents, and took the necessary measures to protect lives and property. Earlier, Saudi-led Coalition spokesperson Major General Turki Al Malki said a tower in the financial district had been targeted and that authorities were responding at the site.

"It is learnt that two Indian nationals have sustained injuries in the attack in Riyadh today. The Embassy is ascertaining further details. All possible assistance will be extended to the injured persons and their families."

— Indian Embassy in Riyadh, in a post on X

Second strike on the district in a week

The attack was the second on the financial district's towers in less than a week. The same tower was struck on November 19 in an attack that damaged the building but caused no injuries, according to reports of that incident. The Houthis have in the past claimed responsibility for attacks on Riyadh; no claim of responsibility for Tuesday's attack had been reported by the time the official statements were issued.

A pattern of risk for Indian workers in the Gulf

Tuesday's injuries come weeks after another attack touched the Indian community in Saudi Arabia directly. An Indian national who was critically injured in the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport died of his injuries on November 4, the Indian Embassy said at the time; 11 Indians were among those injured in that attack. Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate populations in the world, concentrated in construction, services and the financial sector, and the embassy in Riyadh is the first point of contact for families after incidents of this kind.

What to know if you are in Saudi Arabia

The Indian Embassy has asked Indian nationals residing in Saudi Arabia to abide by local rules and regulations. It has not announced any change to consular services. Families of the two injured Indians can reach the embassy in Riyadh, which said it is ascertaining further details and will extend all possible assistance to the injured persons and their families.
